ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A,B,C$ are on circle $\odot O$. If $\angle BAC=40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $ \because \angle BOC=2\angle BAC$ and $\angle BAC=40^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOC=\boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and the three points A, B, C are on the circumference; from A to B and C respectively there are chords AB and AC connected, forming the inscribed angle ∠BAC. O is marked inside the circle as the center of the circle, and OB and OC are connected, forming the central angle ∠BOC. Reasoning: It is known that ∠BAC = 40°. ∠BAC and ∠BOC both correspond to the same set of endpoints B, C, that is, the same arc BC. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the central angle subtended by the same arc is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle, so ∠BOC = 2 × 40° = 80°.

Since both ∠BAC and ∠BOC subtend the same endpoints B and C on the circle, apply the theorem that the central angle is twice the inscribed angle standing on the same arc. Compute ∠BOC = 2 × 40° = 80°.
